checks: Use the linear part of the ordinary ball normalization and its preimage p of zero, which belongs to K. Apply exactly the same affine map to L. Translating the Minkowski sum commutes with the determinant-volume calculation.
A unit-ball capsule along a diametral segment has volume κ_m+κ_(m−1) diam(L′), including the interval case. Its containment in the Minkowski sum proves the stated bound H.

Maximum simplex normalization yields volume ≥ |L′|/(2^m m!). Hadamard bounds each opposite facet area by H^(m−1)/(m−1)!, so the altitude is ≥ aκ_m/(2^m H^(m−1)) and the centroid distance is that altitude divided by m+1.

Combining the two ball sandwiches and pulling back gives the exact constants c and H. Difference bodies preserve these bounds, and fixed constants imply equality of the zero-width directions in every Hausdorff limit, also for point limits.
Source c0cb4d49afb99df3 §§1–2 supplies the same constants and scopes the map to ordinary Euclidean geometry.
